messages:
anya: heads-up - found a correctness bug where eviction metadata compaction produced a schema that older cache nodes interpret as lower "evict_score", causing premature demote of hot prefixes in mixed-version clusters.
kevin: ouch. mixed-version rollout issue?
anya: exactly. new compaction packs fields into a compact blob without a schema version. older nodes deserialize and default missing fields to 0, which lowers computed hotness.
maria: which paths are affected? routing, scoring, or handoff?
anya: scoring + handoff. the handoff logic uses the serialized metadata to decide residency; if score is low a prefix gets demoted even though traffic shows it's hot.
tle: what's the short-term mitigation? can we revert the compaction change?
samir: we already flagged the compaction behind a feature flag for canary, but some infra hosts pulled the flag during scaling. short-term: flip feature off cluster-wide and roll back the compaction encoder.
kevin: rollback plan OK, but we need a fix that won't regress memory.
anya: proposed fix: 1) add explicit schema_version to serialized metadata 2) preserve additive defaults when decoding unknown versions (treat missing fields as "preserve-old-value" not zero) 3) write a migration tool to backfill blobs in object storage for nodes that won't be upgraded soon.
maria: add telemetry: count of "metadata.decode_defaults_used", per-prefix evict_score drift, and a gating alert if demote rate spikes vs traffic by >2x.
tle: long-term idea: make metadata self-describing with a small type-tagged TLV layout so future changes are safe. also include a checksum to detect corrupt compactions.
samir: implementation notes: decoder must support three modes: strict (fail on unknown), compat (ignore unknown but preserve old), and repair (try to reconstruct using migration map). default compat for rollouts.
kevin: how will handoff react during upgrade? we must avoid transient regressions where half the nodes have the new compacted blob and half don't.
anya: plan: staged rollout with validation: after upgrade, run a canary that compares computed evict_score from old vs new decode on sampled prefixes. only promote if divergence < 1% for 30m. also a migration batch to rewrite blobs to new format after cluster reaches stable version.
maria: tests: unit tests for decoding old/new blobs, fuzz test for TLV parser, and an integration canary that simulates mixed-version cluster and asserts no >1% regression in hot-prefix availability.
tle: operationally, add a read-only probe that reads serialized metadata and runs both decoders, emitting a diff metric. handy for rollout gating.
samir: code snippet for compat decoder: 
```
// pseudo
meta = decode(blob)
if meta.missing("evict_score"):
  meta.evict_score = lookup_previous_score(prefix_id) // preserve
return meta
```
kevin: preserve via lookup hits storage - could be expensive. better: include a small inlined "legacy_score" field during compaction when present. fallback lookup only for rare misses.
anya: agreed. we'll include legacy_score when compacting. migration will bulk-insert legacy_score into rewritten blobs.
le: (typo) tle: also ensure compaction is idempotent; multiple runs must not change content.
infra-bot: rollback of compaction encoder completed by @deploy-bot at 11:02 UTC, deploy id rwd-stg-evict-compact-011.
anya: owners: i'll open the schema_version + compat-decoder PR (aim EOD), maria will add telemetry + alerts, tle will draft TLV RFC and idempotency checklist, samir will own migration tool and canary harness.
kevin: please include a runbook step for rapid flip of compaction flag and for how to detect and repair affected blobs.
anya: noted. posting PR links and canary results when ready. thanks.
